subject.title: Self-host: local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access (follow-up to #95 / #104)

question: Should ClawRouter support an opt-in local console authentication mode for the Docker self-host profile, backed by the existing admin-token authority but refused on Cloudflare Access deployments?
rationale: This adds a supported authentication mode and configuration surface rather than repairing an existing documented contract, and it changes the product/security boundary for self-host operators.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in local-auth mode
options.body: Review the linked PR as the implementation path, retaining explicit enablement and refusal whenever Cloudflare Access configuration is present.

options.title: Keep self-host API-only
options.body: Retain the current bearer-token management workflow and decline browser-console sessions for the supported self-host profile.

options.title: Defer to an external integration
options.body: Keep core self-hosting API-only until a separate extension approach can meet the console session requirements without broadening core auth.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in local-auth mode
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR as the implementation path, retaining explicit enablement and refusal whenever Cloudflare Access configuration is present.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged Docker self-host profile and its documented authentication limitation.
